analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one troubleshooting row near head line 2316. The row documents that a cold load can be refused with a 503 or insufficient-memory error when an idle model is resident but held by an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. It describes the hold as excluded from eviction (ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel) and given no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit (autopilotHeldWeightBytes). Nothing executable changed, so no control was altered, weakened or bypassed. I examined the two supplied head-text units, which cover the surrounding inference doc at lines 1209-2033; the changed row sits at about line 2316, outside the supplied text. I checked this documentation against the relevant T-041 definition. The prefix-cache, SSD tier, cacheSalt scoping, TTL and kill-switch text in the supplied sections is unchanged context, so I raised no threat-model gap. The documented behavior is availability-related: a placement hold can make a cold load fail while another model is held. It is a documented behavioral limit, not a new attack surface. A consumer cannot trigger a hold, and the hold's authority and source are outside the supplied evidence. Open question for integration: the Autopilot placement code (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift) and model-autopilot.md were not supplied, so I could not verify that the doc matches the implementation. Any DoS exposure from who can create or extend holds would need review where that code changes. No finding is warranted from this documentation-only diff.
